title: Repair complete V4 replay and directional P10.2 parity
goal: Bind complete supplemental providers, compare module-owned V3 to V4 semantics without hiding weakening, fix exit-16 result parsing and rerun P10.2 once on new paths.
acceptanceCriteria: All frozen identities, 52 Target fingerprints and receipted provider adapter hashes match before execution.
Supplemental provider policies and module-root fingerprints are bound and every current V4 replay equals its certified semantics.
The independent comparator scopes clean rows to module-owned rules and records every V4 fail-closed strengthening separately from exact equivalence.
No V4 acceptance, severity weakening, missing expected rule, empty finding semantics, stale input or unclassified difference remains.
Real clean and violation runs provide structured results with expected exits 0 and 16 respectively.
Protected roots remain byte-invariant and P10.3 plus all activation and cutover boundaries remain false.
risks: Treating all differences as strengthening could conceal a V4 weakening.
Replaying TargetRoot without its suite-local provider could produce false certified drift.
Parsing only one process stream could misclassify an expected blocking exit as engine failure.
Editing frozen engines or prior evidence would invalidate the version ledger.
decisions: Bind provider adapters and policy fixtures in addition to TargetRoot for supplemental cases.
Require local provider adapter bytes to equal the receipted installation adapter.
Use directional non-weakening semantics and preserve explicit strengthening records.
Derive module-owned rules from certified violation rows and keep unrelated V3 findings visible.
Parse structured host results from stdout then stderr while retaining exact expected exits.
Keep frozen engines, fixtures, prior evidence and P10.3 outside mutation scope.
